title: Joint Identified Sets for Four Principal Effects under a Budgeted Common Latent Mechanism
banked_reason: D0.5 delivered incremental below field floor; specialized joint identified set remains sound after removing uncertified numerical claims.
gap_reasons: The 24-column identified-set theorem and saturated-corner law establish a genuine but specialized result under deliberately strong global budgets.

Even if those caps check out, the example is synthetic, budget 2 has no external calibration, and general-data computation and sampling inference remain open, limiting the completed package’s practical significance.

The balanced contrast gap and unequal-data policy separation depend on numerical LP bounds reported in tables without the rational multipliers, vertex records, or executable artifacts needed to verify them.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived an exact two-envelope, 24-column simultaneous identified-set representation and a treatment-labeled saturated-corner law for its declared global-budget subclass. Review placed that sound analytic package at incremental tier, below the field floor. Two numerical contrast and policy-separation propositions lacked reproducible certificates; they and their dependent claims were removed before banking.
tldr: Which four principal effects can one randomized binary-response population realize under one globally budgeted latent mechanism? The answer is an exact two-envelope union of 24-column LP images enforcing every observed mixture, with bounded latent witnesses and a treatment-labeled saturated-corner law at the corrected \(1/18\) radius. Scientific use requires separate calibration of the deliberately stronger budgets; joint E-values are defined only for prespecified effect targets.
gap: Scalar common-\(U\) sensitivity bounds of Chen--Harhay--Li and parametric PI-violation regions of Wu--Antonelli do not give the four-effect identified set under atomwise symmetric selection and global success/failure budgets. A common latent variable by itself is established, not the novelty.
fill: Characterize the exact vector set and finite witnesses; prove the corrected saturated-corner law and certified contrast gaps; show a synthetic, prespecified five percentage-point decision change on unequal data; provide an explicit calibration rule and retain empirical validation as an open question.
